html:
The Tla'amin, once called the Sliammon, are a Northern Coast Salish people of the upper Sunshine Coast of British Columbia, around today's Powell River. ɬaʔamɩn gɩǰɛ is the name of their homeland in their own language.

They fished salmon and herring, gathered shellfish and hunted along the inlets and islands of the northern Strait of Georgia. They are close kin of the Klahoose and Homalco, with whom they were known as the Mainland Comox. A paper mill was built on their main village site at Powell River in the early 1900s. Their modern treaty with Canada and British Columbia took effect in 2016.
